verdict.rationale: ScrapingBee's JavaScript scenario feature lets developers add interaction instructions to an API call before the HTML is returned. The documented example shows clicking (wait_for_and_click), filling inputs (fill), waiting and scrolling (scroll_y), and the API can also wait for a selector before returning. One documented limitation is that infinite_scroll is not supported with stealth_proxy. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that scenarios work reliably, and fuller evidence of the complete instruction set and its limits.

support.subject: As a developer, I can script page interactions like clicking, filling inputs, and scrolling before content is returned

citations.quote: If you want to interact with pages you want to scrape before we return your the HTML you can add JavaScript scenario to your API call.
Our headless browsers will wait for the CSS / Xpath selector passed in the parameter before returning the HTML.
